To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the strain at a notch tip is independent of the path around the notch and that the path independent strain integral can be expressed in terms either of the stress intensity factor or of the concentrated deformation at the notch tip.
A path independent integral, which is the line integral along a closed path of a function of stress and displacement, is exhibited which has a unique value for all paths encircling a notch.

a path independent integral may be evaluated, in terms of the stress intensity factor, for elastic plastic materials that are linearly elastic in the vicinity of a notch tip and that yield on a scale small relative to the notch tip radius.

the analysis of strain concentrations in elastic and elastic-plastic materials and their application to fracture problems.
the development and application of path independent integrals in the study of elastic, elastic plastic and plastic deformation fields.
